name: CA-38
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's +8 Democratic partisan lean after redistricting
Solis's large fundraising and outside-support advantage over Casas
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near certainty
model.rationale: The fundamentals point clearly to Democrats: the redrawn district leans +8 Democratic in a favorable national environment, and Hilda Solis has raised over $1 million with outside support while Pedro Casas reports no measurable fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win at roughly 98%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected Republican fundraising surge could narrow the expected margin, though a flip in outcome remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
The 38th District of California is an open seat after redistricting, with no incumbent on the ballot. County supervisor Hilda Solis, a well-known Democrat, faces Republican Pedro Casas in a district that leans about eight points Democratic. Solis has raised more than $1 million and benefits from outside spending, while Casas shows no reported fundraising. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race.

Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability near 98 percent, and the fundamentals-based estimate points to a Democratic margin near 20 points. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of competition.
